title: The Ai Trick for Consistent 2D Game Assets
author: FutureTechPilot
selftext:
**TLDR:** The trick for consistent 2D assets is to ask Codex (GPT) to draw the asset \*on to\* an existing screenshot - then you isolate the asset after - and you can place it wherever you want

1. If you try to generate assets using only your words, you'll never achieve consistency - and even if you use a reference image, you're not guaranteed success - the trick I found to work best is to give GPT a screenshot of my game and ask it to draw a new asset on top of the screenshot. 

2. Then you have to ask the model (GPT in this case) to isolate the new asset - I used a prompt like this "**Take the chicken coop with its fenced run and chickens from this game screenshot. Show it alone, exactly as it is drawn in this image - same art style, colours, ink lines, shading, angle and proportions - with nothing else from the scene, centered on a flat solid magenta background**"

\^ you may need to adjust the colors after - I had Opus 5.5 write a script to change the saturation/brightness to match the rest of the game

And there are some more tips you can try like:

\- Remember to ask for variety (or all your carrots will look the same)

\- Ask for life cycles of certain assets

\- Do your best to describe what the asset \*actually\* is, rather than just the name (I know this tip kinda sucks and is kinda confusing, but hopefully you'll understand what I mean - check the video above to see an example of the 'Shipping Bin')

Anyways, hope that helps a bit. 

Cheers, 

\- Nolan

comments.author: RapidOSRS
comments.body:
Couldn't you just include some reference art in the process? That's what I do. I have reference art-style, in a file, and a list of assets I need, with descriptions written based on tested creation prompts, size requirements, etc

  
Then Opus 5.5 sends it off to Codex using 6.1 Sol - High, gets it back, reviews it, and makes numeric markups, cutouts, and text prompts, to correct it, to get it within an accepted rate for what we'd except (usually 93% correct) with a retry limit. 

Then again I've built a whole production factory for assets and I'm very strict, because I refuse to post my game if the art looks like AI slop.
